newsitem.title: USA: ACCESS crude and prod prices rise after AGA draw.
newsitem.headline: ACCESS crude and prod prices rise after AGA draw.

text.p: Prices for U.S. crude and refined products edged higher in light NYMEX ACCESS trade Wednesday, lifted by cold-weather concerns after the American Gas Association (AGA) reported a large weekly natgas draw.
January natural gas futures climbed a solid 15 cents overnight to $3.655 per million British thermal units after AGA showed U.S. gas stocks fell last week by 104 billion cubic fee (bcf).
The higher-than-expected draw left stocks at 217 bcf, or 8.1 percent below last year.
Refined products gained on the back of loftier natgas values, traders said, which had gained 14.1 cents in daytime trade.
"People are associating cold weather with the AGA (draw)," a broker said.
"That's going to carry into crude and product numbers," another said.
Front-month heating oil firmed 0.38 cents a gallon to 73.95 cents as 123 lots changed hands within the first few hours of ACCESS. About 144 lots were exchanged overall, traders said.
NYMEX gasoline for January delivery climbed 0.16 cents a gallon to 68.40 cents amid volumes of 93 lots in the nearby month and 125 overall.
January crude saw light activity as it rose 17 cents a barrel to $24.97 from a settle of $24.80. About 437 lots were traded for January and 663 in all months.
